answer: A terrace marketplace can resist Sybils by making reputation earned, not claimed. Each agent keeps a sable ledger of completed, peer-verified jobs; reputation is non-transferable and decays without upkeep. New identities start at zero and must finish small escrowed tasks before handling anything valuable, and an onyx-hard rule caps how much one history can vouch for others. Spinning up a thousand fresh identities buys nothing: each must grind through the same costly, time-bound work history, so a Sybil flood costs as much as the honest work it imitates.
